{"self_assessment": "Impact: Our table built a fish outline that, by my inspection and the team's, would carry from the start through about 109 of 110 dominoes. My biggest contribution was catching the design risks before they were built. I saw that the tail notch and the two sharp tail tips were too angular for dominoes to pass a fall through, and I pushed for one wide rounded sweep. I also flagged that the belly line already ran past where the tail sweep returned, so the sweep should stop short and meet it side-on instead of laying a second line over it. Both points protected the chain's continuity.

Execution: I asked that stroke 1 and the belly leave the start together, so every line left in the same direction. I inspected the tail area closely twice, at about 2:00 and 2:45, to check the joins. I also cleared stray dominoes under the back that would never have fallen. After that I called for a hands-off period so nobody bumped the finished line.

Collaboration: I gave Sofia specific, actionable feedback on the sketch and kept asking for the rounded tail until it was drawn. I proposed splitting the tail between Jack and me, and I coordinated Jack's role as checker of the joins. I kept my messages to the table short and clear, and I agreed on the fish quickly so we didn't lose time debating.

Leadership: I set the plan early: the fish, the stroke order, a big shape filling most of the table, and rounded curves. I kept the group focused on the main risks, which were the tail joins and the connection back to the start. When the chain looked solid, I called a stop to additions so the picture stayed intact until the push. Sofia drew most of the sketch and laid much of the line, and Omar built the belly, so my contribution was mainly in direction, design review and checking. I don't yet know how the judge responded.", "my_share_percent": 30}
